ted byte-for-byte as before. Verified: the 96-line fixture CSV contains **zero** `"` characters and no CRLF.

## Test — `tests/test_export.py::test_export_month_quotes_fields_that_contain_the_separator`

Customer `Zed; Inc "Z"` round-trips through `csv.reader(delimiter=";")` to 7 columns with the name intact, and a plain-invoice line is asserted unquoted so the documented format can't silently drift into universal quoting.

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest -q` → **14 passed**.
- Independent audit before the change: all 95 fixture rows' `net/vat/gross` matched a `Fraction`-based exact half-even recomputation, **0 mismatches** — so the numbers were already right; this was the only remaining format hole.
- Signatures unchanged: `compute(net, country)`, `export_month(invoices, year, month, outdir)`.

One residual: a `;`-free customer name containing a raw newline would still quote into a multi-line field. The spec has no rule for it, so I left it alone — say the word if you want a belt-and-braces normalisation instead.
